The dominant fact in this profile is degree: avg_degree 736.5 with density 0.1233 on only 11944 nodes, so every node's neighbourhood covers a large share of the graph. That disqualifies the whole neighbour-relative family by its own stated failure mode. local_affinity and homophily_violation both average neighbour rows, and over ~736 neighbours that average is the global mean for everyone; the local_affinity landmarker confirms it, being a near-symmetric bulk (mean 0.5035, p50 0.5288, p99 only 0.8825) with no separated tail, which is the shape of a view that has lost resolution rather than found a mechanism. attr_struct_mismatch inherits that dead half, so its wide spread (p90 0.7402) is what a rank difference against a noisy ranking looks like, not evidence. reconstruction is neighbourhood-smoothed by the same decoder aggregation and degenerates for the same reason. spectral, above 3000 nodes, reduces to the residual of one-hop smoothing, and at this density one-hop smoothing removes almost nothing; it also sees only the attribute norm, not its direction. community is blocked from the other side: modularity 0.2485 is below the ~0.3 threshold where a partition is meaningful, and 7 communities over 11944 nodes means centroids sitting near the global mean, with the normalisation by community spread erasing the remainder. Note also that homophily = 0.4967 is only Louvain co-membership, so the gates it opened for the two neighbour-relative views carry no attribute evidence at all. What survives are views whose reference frame is not the neighbourhood. one_class is first because it judges each node against a single global centre, so high degree cannot dilute it, while its GCN layers still let dense structure and 25-dimensional attributes inform the embedding; its risk here is embedding collapse, not degree. density is the natural complement because it reads no edges whatsoever and is therefore fully immune to the degree problem, and its preconditions hold: feature_dim 25 is low enough that nearest-neighbour distances do not concentrate, and feature_sparsity 0.4156 is moderate rather than the binary-sparse regime where LOF fails. Its landmarker is the most promising shape on offer, a tight mass near zero (p50 0.0076) with a thin upper tail reaching 0.0602 at p99, roughly eight times the median. contrastive is third as the only remaining independent axis, per-node embedding stability under attribute dropout in a globally trained space; feature_sparsity 0.4156 and feature_dup_rate 0.1762 are moderate, so dropout on a 25-dimensional row still perturbs something, though the 17.6% template rows are the reason it ranks third rather than second. adversarial is left out as the redundant global GCN view next to one_class, with an added saturation risk. The three chosen cover a global embedding boundary, a graph-free attribute-space view, and an embedding-stability view, with no two sharing a reference frame.

What survives are the views whose reference frame is global or edge-free. one_class judges each node against the bulk of all nodes from a single centre, so neighbourhood convergence does not erase its contrast; its only stated failure, embedding collapse, is not indicated by anything in the profile, and no landmarker exists to contradict it. density is the one paradigm that never reads the edges, so it is structurally immune to the degree problem, and feature_dim = 25 with feature_sparsity = 0.4156 is low-dimensional and not sparse enough for distance concentration, so LOF retains meaning; its landmarker is crushed at the bottom with an extreme thin tail (p50 0.0076, p95 0.0299, p99 0.0602), which is a small set of genuine attribute-space outliers rather than a graded field. adversarial adds a second global discriminative view that reads structure, complementing LOF's edge-blind attribute view, with the caveat that saturation is not something this profile can rule out. contrastive is left out on its own degeneracy clause: feature_sparsity 0.4156 plus feature_dup_rate 0.1762 means attribute dropout perturbs a redundant, partly templated 25-dim row very little, so most nodes would read as stable.

That disqualifies local_affinity, homophily_violation and, by inheritance of its neighbour-relative half, attr_struct_mismatch; their landmarkers agree, local_affinity sitting at mean 0.5035 with p99 only 0.8825 and no separated upper tail, which is the shape of a diffuse ranking rather than a mechanism. reconstruction fails for the same reason: a GCN decoder aggregating over 736 neighbours reconstructs nearly every node from the same smoothed signal. community is also out, modularity = 0.2485 is below the 0.3 threshold where a partition means anything, and with only 7 communities over 11944 nodes each centroid is close to the global mean, which the per-community normalisation then flattens further; homophily = 0.4967 is barely above chance for this partition, confirming the structure is not cleanly clustered. spectral reduces 25 attributes to one scalar norm and, at this density, one-hop smoothing removes almost nothing, so its residual is close to a raw magnitude ranking.
